title: Sphinx
html_source: That Stephen thinks of the Sphinx here is probably Joyce inserting either a subconscious reaction by Stephen to the setting, or is a way of sneaking in another hidden commentary on this whole surreal scene. Joyce here alludes to Oscar Wilde’s The Sphinx, and Don Gifford points us to the Sphinx’s being address as “exquisite grotesque! half woman and half animal.” The poem’s speaker rejects her as the creature of a “songless tongueless ghost of sin crept through the curtains of the night… Get hence, you loathsome mystery! Hideous animal, get hence!” he commands. “You wake in me each bestial sense, you make me what I would not be.”
